items.abstract: Penelitian ini menyajikan eksperimen penulisan jarak jauh untuk menganalisis secara komparatif representasi kota Makassar dalam dua korpus sastra yang berbeda: karya yang ditulis oleh manusia dan teks yang dihasilkan oleh Kecerdasan Buatan (AI). Maraknya penggunaan AI dalam produksi kreatif memicu pertanyaan epistemologis mendasar mengenai kepengarangan dan kapasitas mesin untuk menggambarkan entitas budaya. Makassar, dengan karakteristik sosio-spasialnya yang unik, berfungsi sebagai studi kasus untuk menguji perbedaan antara representasi yang didorong oleh pengalaman manusia dan yang berasal dari algoritma.Dengan memanfaatkan Large Language Models (LLMs) seperti ChatGPT menggunakan perintah yang identik dan dirancang dengan cermat, penelitian ini akan mengumpulkan korpus AI untuk disandingkan secara langsung dan kritis dengan korpus sastra yang sudah ada yang ditulis oleh manusia.Dengan menerapkan analisis teks komputasi tingkat lanjut (pemodelan topik, stilometri, analisis sentimen/leksikal) bersamaan dengan pembacaan cermat (close reading) secara kualitatif, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk membedakan pola tematik, stilistik, dan linguistik yang unik di dalam masing-masing korpus. Temuan yang diantisipasi akan menjelaskan kemampuan dan keterbatasan generatif AI dalam memproduksi konten yang bernuansa budaya, mengungkap potensi bias dalam data pelatihan, dan berkontribusi secara substansial pada konsep kreativitas dan representasi urban digital yang terus berkembang, terutama di bidang Humaniora Digital dan estetika komputasional.

items.title: Machine Learning-Based Vulnerability Detection in AI-Generated Source Code: A Systematic Literature Review and Research Directions
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of Generative AI and Large Language Models (LLMs) has transformed software development, but AI-generated code may contain security vulnerabilities such as injection flaws, weak authentication, and unsafe API usage. Traditional rule-based and static-analysis techniques struggle with semantically diverse generated code. This paper presents a systematic literature review of Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), Graph Neural Network, Transformer, and LLM-based vulnerability detection, with emphasis on AI-generated source code. It compares approaches, datasets, and code representations, and examines challenges including data imbalance, false positives, limited AI-generated datasets, and explainability. A conceptual framework combining preprocessing, structural and semantic representation, ML/DL classification, CWE categorization, explainability, and validation is proposed. Future directions include hybrid ML-LLM models, real-time IDE integration, and automated vulnerability repair..

items.title: Make or buy AI? Evidence on AI sourcing decisions and workforce outcomes
items.abstract: We examine how firms acquire artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities and how their AI sourcing decisions relate to workforce outcomes. Using Swedish enterprise surveys from 2019 and 2021 linked to financial statements and employer–employee data, we directly observe whether firms adopt AI and whether they outsource AI-related activities. AI adoption is concentrated among larger firms. Among adopters, pre-existing cost pressure is associated with outsourcing. Relative to non-adopters, both in-house adopters and outsourcers have higher subsequent employment and persistently higher shares of university-educated and computer-science (CS)-educated workers, with no further change in workforce composition in the year after adoption. Workforce outcomes are statistically indistinguishable between in-house adopters and outsourcers.

items.title: Mapping Digital and Experiential Project-Based Learning in STEM Education: A Scientometric Analysis of Curriculum, Engagement and Research Fronts
items.abstract: Digital and experiential project-based learning (PBL) has become a prominent response to the demand for authentic, technology-mediated STEM instruction, yet existing bibliometric mappings of this literature have been confined to a single database, a single educational level or a window shorter than a decade. This study reports a scientometric analysis of the field for 2015-2024. A five-facet Boolean query was executed in Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection in April 2025. After removal of ineligible document types (n = 230) and cross-database duplicates (n = 666), 2,103 records were analysed in ScientoPy 2.1.3 using total output, average growth rate (AGR), average documents per year (ADY) and percentage of documents published in the last years (PDLY). Journal articles (n = 930) and conference papers (n = 757) dominated; review articles, although few (n = 68), showed the highest recency (PDLY = 25.0%), signalling a field entering consolidation. Author keywords concentrated on “project-based learning” (n = 307), “experiential learning” (n = 221) and “virtual reality” (n = 129), while “online learning” declined (AGR = −2), consistent with terminological migration. The United States led absolute output (n = 594), but Indonesia (PDLY = 44.8%) and India (PDLY = 30.3%) accelerated most steeply. Individual and institutional productivity was flat and unconcentrated: no author exceeded eight documents and no institution exceeded nine. The study contributes the first decade-scale, two-database performance and thematic map of digital PBL in STEM education and identifies assessment methodology, artificial-intelligence integration and cross-system comparative work as principal research fronts.

items.title: Masculine honor, social visibility, and safety non-compliance: intentions and approval judgments in high-risk sectors in Turkey
items.abstract: Unsafe work in high-risk sectors cannot be explained only by knowledge deficits or weak safety management; workers may also attach reputational meaning to visible compliance. Drawing on honor theory and occupational-safety research on risk perception and social context, this study examined whether masculine honor values (hereafter honor values)—the belief that a man’s worth depends partly on a publicly defensible reputation—were associated with unsafe work intentions, lower perceived risk, and greater approval of safety-rule non-compliance among male workers in Turkish construction and shipbuilding. A worker survey (N = 244) was combined with a within-person vignette experiment in which the focal hazard was held constant while visibility was manipulated and audience identity and prior social comment varied orthogonally. Honor values were positively associated with unsafe work intentions (H1a) and approval of others’ violations (H1b), and negatively associated with perceived risk (H2). Perceived risk partially accounted for the honor–intention association (H3). The association between honor values and approval of non-compliance was stronger when the violation was public rather than private (H4), consistent with a reputational, visibility-contingent account. These findings identify a micro-level sociocultural pathway that complements knowledge- and risk-based accounts of safety decisions. They also suggest that safety communication and supervisory practice should address the social meaning of compliance, while the cross-sectional mediation and judgment-based vignette outcome limit causal and behavioral inference.

items.abstract: We study the structural, thermophysical, and dynamical properties of molten MgCl2 over a wide temperature range using Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics (AIMD) and molecular dynamics simulations based on machine-learning interaction potentials (MLIPs). MLIPs can achieve near-AIMD accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost, enabling simulations of larger systems and longer timescales. This opens up the possibility of studying the system under out-of-equilibrium conditions, which in turn allows for the calculation of physical properties, such as the thermal conductivity or viscosity, that cannot be obtained reliably for the typical time and length scales accessible to AIMD. We follow two complementary approaches to develop and evaluate the MLIPs. First, we develop a Deep Potential (DP) from scratch using AIMD trajectories at different temperatures. Second, we also evaluate two out-of-the-box foundation models and a fine-tuned version of one of them. The fine-tuning is performed using configurations from the AIMD trajectories originally used to train the DP. We compare the predictions of the trained DP, the foundation models, and AIMD simulations with the available experimental data and provide a comprehensive calculation of the most important physical quantities of molten MgCl2. We compute densities, radial and angular distribution functions, thermal conductivity, heat capacity, viscosity, and diffusion coefficients over the 1000–1600 K temperature range. This range is relevant to important technological applications such as thermal energy storage, generation IV nuclear reactors, and concentrated solar power systems. Finally, we briefly review the accuracy and performance of the different MLIP versions used throughout the work.

items.title: MEASURING STUDENTS' INFORMATION SECURITY COMPETENCE IN THE CONTEXT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: CRITERIA, INDICATORS AND RELIABILITY OF THE DIAGNOSTIC TOOLKIT
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education has created new opportunities for learning while increasing the complexity of information security risks faced by university students. These risks include phishing, identity theft, unauthorized disclosure of personal data, manipulated digital content, and the uncritical use of AI-generated information. Consequently, assessing students’ information security competence requires an approach that extends beyond theoretical knowledge and incorporates practical skills, risk assessment, responsible digital behaviour, and the critical evaluation of AI-generated outputs. This article proposes a multidimensional diagnostic assessment framework for measuring students’ information security competence in AI-supported educational environments. The framework comprises five criteria: cognitive, operational, analytical, behavioural, and ethical-legal. For each criterion, observable indicators and appropriate assessment methods are specified. The article also outlines procedures for evaluating the reliability and validity of the proposed diagnostic instruments, including internal consistency analysis, test–retest reliability, expert evaluation, and construct validation. The framework is informed by established digital competence and AI competence frameworks, as well as recognized principles of educational measurement. Since the proposed model has not been empirically validated within the scope of this article, its psychometric properties are presented as matters for future investigation rather than established findings. The proposed approach provides a methodological basis for developing evidence-based assessment instruments for higher education.

items.title: MEASURING THE GAP: A FOUR-BENCHMARK COMPARATIVE ASSESSMENT OF AI-DRIVEN BANKING FRAUD LAW IN INDIA, THE USA, AND THE UK
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has altered the way banks are defrauded, though not, in most jurisdictions, the legal text that governs it. This paper offers a comparative doctrinal analysis of the legal and regulatory framework for AI-driven banking fraud in India, the United States, and the United Kingdom against four benchmarks: coverage (whether legal definitions capture AI-specific fraud mechanisms), attributability (whether liability can be fixed on a human actor or institution when AI is involved), enforceability (whether investigative and supervisory tools can handle AI-mediated evidence), and proportionality (whether penalties and remedies match the harm AI-enabled fraud causes). Applying these benchmarks to primary law, regulatory instruments, and decided and pending case law, the paper finds that no jurisdiction scores strongly on all four. The United Kingdom leads on coverage and enforceability but is only partial on attributability and proportionality; the United States is strong on enforceability but unsettled on the other three; and India is weak on enforceability and proportionality while, like the United States, untested rather than deficient on coverage and attributability. The paper argues that the binary of a 'reactive' India against 'proactive' Western comparators is misleading: the three jurisdictions are converging on a sectoral, regulator-led model and differ chiefly in the institutional durability of their rule-making processes, not in the protectiveness of the rules those processes produce.

items.abstract: Medication safety remains a major priority in contemporary healthcare systems because medication-related harm can occur across the entire medication-use process, including prescribing, dispensing, administration, monitoring, and patient self-management.Digital health technologies have created new opportunities to reduce preventable medication errors and improve pharmaceutical care.This comprehensive narrative review examines the role of electronic prescribing, computerized provider order entry, clinical decision support systems, artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, digital pharmacovigilance, telepharmacy, mobile health applications, barcode medication administration, smart infusion pumps, automated dispensing systems, and closed-loop medication management in improving medication safety.The review also provides a critical appraisal of evidence, highlighting that many digital interventions reduce process-related errors, whereas fewer studies demonstrate consistent reductions in severe patient-centered outcomes.Digital medication safety is best understood as a sociotechnical process requiring pharmacist expertise, workflow integration, high-quality data, clinical governance, cybersecurity, patient engagement, and continuous evaluation.Pharmacists have a central role in validating prescriptions, optimizing alerts, interpreting artificial intelligence outputs, maintaining smart pump libraries, supporting telepharmacy, improving pharmacovigilance, and educating patients.Digital technologies can strengthen medication safety when they support, rather than replace, professional judgment and patient-centered care.

items.title: Model Risk-Based AI Governance dalam pendidikan tinggi Indonesia: Rekonstruksi kebijakan untuk mewujudkan integritas akademik
items.abstract: Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dalam pendidikan tinggi menimbulkan kebutuhan untuk membangun tata kelola yang mampu mengakomodasi manfaat teknologi sekaligus melindungi integritas akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis kesenjangan tata kelola pemanfaatan AI dalam pendidikan tinggi Indonesia dan merumuskan model kebijakan berbasis risiko yang membedakan penggunaan AI berdasarkan tingkat risiko serta menentukan kewajiban, pembatasan, pengawasan, dan pertanggungjawaban yang proporsional. Permasalahan penelitian berfokus pada bagaimana kebijakan pemanfaatan AI dapat direkonstruksi melalui pendekatan Risk-Based AI Governance untuk membedakan penggunaan asistif, bersyarat, terbatas, dan tidak dapat diterima. Penelitian ini merupakan penelitian hukum normatif dengan pendekatan perundang-undangan, konseptual, dan perbandingan melalui studi kepustakaan serta analisis kualitatif-yuridis terhadap peraturan, kebijakan, pedoman, dan literatur terkait. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa regulasi Indonesia telah menyediakan prinsip kehati-hatian, keamanan, transparansi, akuntabilitas, perlindungan data, pengawasan, dan manajemen risiko, tetapi belum mengintegrasikannya dalam klasifikasi risiko AI yang spesifik untuk pendidikan tinggi. Penelitian menghasilkan model empat tingkat risiko yang terhubung dengan differentiated controls, human oversight, transparency/disclosure, monitoring dan audit, evaluasi, mitigasi, serta remediasi atau sanksi, dengan integritas akademik sebagai tujuan normatif utama.

items.title: MonoRace: Robust monocular AI for champion-level drone racing
items.abstract: Autonomous drone racing represents a major frontier in robotics research. It requires an artificial intelligence (AI) that can run onboard lightweight flying robots under tight resource and time constraints while pushing the physical system to its limits. The state of the art in this area consists of a system with a stereo camera and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) that beat human drone-racing champions in a controlled indoor environment. Here, we present MonoRace, an onboard drone-racing approach that generalizes to a competition environment without any external motion tracking system, using only a monocular rolling-shutter camera and an IMU. The approach features robust state estimation that combines neural network–based gate segmentation with a drone model. Moreover, it includes an offline optimization procedure that leverages the known geometry of gates to refine any state estimation parameter. This offline optimization is based purely on onboard flight data and is important for fine-tuning the extrinsic camera calibration parameters. Furthermore, the guidance and control are performed by a neural network that forgoes inner-loop controllers by directly sending motor commands. This small network runs on the flight controller at 500 hertz. The proposed approach won the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Drone Racing Competition 2025, outperforming all competing autonomous drone race teams and three world champion human pilots in a direct knockout tournament. It reached speeds up to 100 kilometers per hour on the competition track and successfully coped with problems such as camera interference and IMU saturation.

items.title: Multi-objective optimized signal decomposition with explainable and reliable hybrid models for multistep significant wave height forecasting in ocean wave energy applications
items.abstract: Accurate forecasting of significant wave height (Hs) is vital for marine safety, coastal engineering, and renewable energy production. This study presents an effective integrated model system to forecast Hs for two distinct sites in Australia, Gladstone and Palm Beach, over various time horizons from 30-min to 24-h ahead during the period of 2018 to 2022. In the first stage, a novel multi-objective Optuna is developed to optimize the decomposition parameters using two criteria of compactness, bandwidth, and peakedness of a signal's frequency spectrum. The proposed methodology is utilized for hyperparameter tuning of Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) and De-mixing Multivariate Variational Mode Decomposition (D-MVMD) techniques. This enables an optimal data decomposition process by eliminating the need for manual parameter selection. In the second stage, an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) approach, SHAPley Additive Explanations (SHAP), is used to identify the most influential components and analyze their interactions. These optimized and interpretable decomposed signals are then used as inputs to standalone forecasting models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), deep Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). These optimized and interpretable decomposed signals are then used as inputs to the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), deep Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models to forecast. In the final stage, a comprehensive Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) is employed to quantify uncertainties and perform reliability analysis. The SHAP-based feature selection reduced the input variables from 37 to 48 decomposed components to a single dominant predictor while maintaining nearly identical predictive accuracy across all forecast horizons, significantly lowering computational costs. Among the models, the SSA-RVFL demonstrated superior performance, with lower computational cost and the highest forecasting accuracy across all time horizons. This model achieved the highest Index of Agreement (IA: 0.81-1) and determination coefficient (R 2 : 0.49-0.98), and lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE: 0.04-0.33) across stations and horizons. In addition, the results confirm operational reliability exceeding 88% for forecasts up to 6 h ahead. Overall, the fully optimized SSA integrated with the SHAP-RVFL-MCS results provides a robust framework for enhancing decision-making in coastal hazard and wave energy planning.

items.title: MULTIMODAL MARKERS OF DIGITAL IDENTITY: THE CONSTRUCTION OF THE SELF AND NEW MODELS OF COMMUNICATION
items.abstract: The article examines multimodal markers of digital identity as means of self-presentation and self-identification in the contemporary communicative environment. Particular attention is paid to the phenomenon of the multimodal turn in digital communication, which has expanded traditional linguistic mechanisms of interaction through the integration of visual, graphic, and paralinguistic means. The role of verbal, visual, and paralinguistic resources in the construction of the digital self and the formation of new models of online self-presentation is analysed. Special attention is devoted to professional, national, social, gender, and generational aspects of digital self-identification. It is demonstrated that digital identity is realised through a complex system of multimodal markers, including photographs, visual symbols, emojis, memes, reactions, intertextual practices, and other means of digital communication. It is substantiated that the meaning of such markers is shaped by the communicative context as well as by users’ age, gender, cultural, professional, and social characteristics. The study establishes that the contextual nature of multimodal markers gives rise to semiotic gaps between different generations, social groups, and digital communities, causing the same sign to acquire different interpretations across communicative environments. Against this background, the article analyses the peculiarities of communication within the Human–AI model, the phenomenon of algorithmic empathy, and the mechanisms of linguistic adaptation employed by generative artificial intelligence systems to users’ communicative practices. It is revealed that multimodal markers function not only as important instruments of identity representation but also as factors in the formation of new models of digital interaction. The study concludes that the widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence transforms not only the mechanisms of digital self-identification but also the very foundations of mutual understanding in contemporary digital society.

items.title: Multimodal wearable biosensors in sports: integrating physical and chemical sensing for performance and health
items.abstract: Wearable technologies have emerged as essential tools for monitoring athletes’ performance and physiological states in real time. This review systematically examines advances in biosensing and wearable systems for sports applications, highlighting their design, sensing modalities, and integration strategies. Athlete tracking and data acquisition form the foundation for personalized training, injury prevention, and performance optimization. Biopotential sensors, including electrocardiography (ECG), electromyography (EMG), electroencephalography (EEG)/electroneurogram Electroneurography, and biopotential electrodes, provide insights into cardiac, muscular, and neural activity. Physical sensors, such as temperature, piezoresistive, piezoelectric, balance and acceleration, pressure, optical, and galvanic skin response (GSR) sensors, enable real-time assessment of movement, mechanical load, body posture, stress, and environmental interactions. Chemical sensors, including sweat and glucose sensors, facilitate non-invasive metabolic monitoring, supporting hydration and energy management. Integrated and hybrid biosensor systems combine multiple sensing modalities, offering comprehensive real-time feedback and personalized analytics for athletes. Despite these advances, challenges remain in sensor miniaturization, power efficiency, data accuracy, wireless communication, and user comfort. Future directions focus on artificial intelligence-driven data analysis, flexible and durable materials, multi-modal integration, and fully personalized wearable platforms. Collectively, wearable biosensing technologies present a transformative approach to sports monitoring, enabling enhanced performance evaluation, injury prevention, and long-term health management.

items.title: Musculoskeletal Disorders and Health‐Related Quality of Life Among Information Technology Professionals in the Post‐Pandemic Period: A Cross‐Sectional Occupational Health Study
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background IT professionals face sustained ergonomic exposures, including prolonged sedentary behaviour, high screen time, and suboptimal workstation design, that intensified following pandemic‐driven shifts to remote and hybrid work. These conditions predispose this occupational cohort to musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and impaired health related quality of life (HRQoL); however, population—specific evidence remains limited. Objective To estimate 12‐month MSD prevalence and regional distribution among IT professionals, compare HRQoL across MSD and non‐MSD groups, and identify factors independently associated with MSDs. Methods A purposive‐stratified cross‐sectional survey was conducted among 1568 full‐time or part‐time IT professionals (aged 20–60 years) recruited from corporate technology firms, software companies, BPO units, and remote working platforms across India with a response rate of 98%. MSD prevalence and disability were assessed using the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ); HRQoL was evaluated using the World Health Organisation Quality of Life (WHOQOL‐BREF) questionnaire. Factors independently associated with MSD presence were identified through multivariable backward stepwise logistic regression (Nagelkerke R 2 reported); MSD severity—HRQoL associations were examined using linear regression. Results The 12‐month prevalence of MSD was 71.4%. The neck (59.2%), lower back (53.7%), and shoulders (46.1%) were most affected. Multi‐regional involvement correlated with significantly greater disability (6.1 ± 2.4 vs. 4.2 ± 1.9; p < 0.001). The MSD group demonstrated markedly lower physical HRQoL (48.3 ± 13.6 vs. 71.9 ± 12.8; p < 0.001), with significant differences across all WHOQOL‐BREF domains. The strongest independent factors associated with MSDs were daily work > 10 hours (OR 2.93, 95% CI 2.10–4.07), poor ergonomic conditions (OR = 2.42, 95% CI 1.99–2.94), and remote work modality (OR = 1.78, 95%CI 1.42–2.21; Nagelkerke R 2 = 0.41). Conclusion MSDs are highly prevalent among IT professionals and are independently associated with impaired HRQoL across all domains. Poor ergonomic conditions, extended work hours, and remote work modality were independently associated with MSD presence and represent potentially modifiable workplace characteristics warranting further evaluation.

items.title: Music Marketing with Generative AI
items.abstract: The multibillion-dollar music industry faces severe content creation bottlenecks, making multimedia marketing assets prohibitively costly for smaller artists. This practice paper introduces a Marketing Asset Generation Engine (MAGE) that can produce over 700 million video ad variations reflecting each artist’s visual identity using only a music track’s audio and album cover as inputs. Collaborating with one of the world’s largest music labels, we conduct four preregistered field studies with over 11 million impressions across 75 campaigns for 33 music tracks on TikTok and Meta to validate MAGE. First, pooled across studies, MAGE-generated ads significantly outperform human-designed ads on TikTok with on average 26% higher click-through rates and 10% higher engagement, while we do not detect statistically significant performance differences on Meta, all at 98% lower production cost. Second, neither marketing professionals nor laypeople can reliably identify winning ads such that random sampling of MAGE’s outputs performs as well as human-curated selections. In contrast, an AI-in-the-loop system trained on past performance data can predict pre-launch which MAGE-generated ads will perform best for specific audience segments. These findings demonstrate that generative AI democratizes music marketing by making effective, on-brand video ads accessible at scale.

items.title: Navigating dual pathways: learning-oriented and instrumental identities in AI-mediated informal digital learning of English
items.abstract: Generative AI is increasingly reshaping how learners engage in informal English learning beyond the classroom, making AI-mediated informal digital learning of English (AI-IDLE) an important emerging learning context. Yet research has predominantly focused on intra-personal psychological factors, the social dimensions of learning, particularly how learners construct their social identities in relation to AI, remain significantly underexplored. This qualitative study examines the social identity categories and their construction processes among 12 Chinese university EFL learners engaged in AI-IDLE. Drawing on Social Identity Theory (SIT), data from semi-structured interviews, reflective journals, and AI chat logs were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings reveal two distinct identity pathways: learning-oriented academic identities, characterized by deep-learning commitment, humble mindset toward AI, and sustained immersion in the student role; and an instrumental identity, organized around a user category defined by transactional engagement, service satisfaction and surface learning approaches. Within this instrumental pathway, a more intensified fast-food consumer orientation emerged, which was explicitly self-identified by one participant and analytically inferred from behavioral patterns across several others. The study demonstrates that AI-IDLE does not simply erase or replace existing social identities but selectively reinforces and reconfigures them through group norms, prototypical markers, and evaluative comparison. These findings extend SIT by revealing how technological affordances and social configuration shape identity pathways that support or undermine meaningful learning engagement. Practical implications are proposed for AI developers, digital learning designers, educators, and curriculum designers to foster learning-oriented identity pathways in AI-mediated informal learning environments

items.title: Needs and current status of generative artificial intelligence use among college students: a cross-sectional survey based in China
items.abstract: Objective This study aimed to investigate the current status of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) usage needs among vocational college students from China, explore their relationships with learning engagement and academic resilience, and identify variables associated with GAI usage demand. Methods Using convenience sampling, 3,876 students from five vocational colleges in Sichuan Province were enrolled. Surveys were conducted using the Generative Artificial Intelligence Application Status and Usage Demand Scale, the Learning Engagement Scale, and the Academic Resilience Scale. Results The average GAI needs score among vocational college students was 58.23 ± 12.77. Correlation analysis revealed positive relationships between GAI needs and both learning engagement and academic resilience ( p < 0.01). Multiple linear regression analysis revealed that gender, academic year, availability of GAI learning devices at home, level of GAI understanding, enrollment in GAI-related courses, frequency of active GAI use, student-reported frequency of teachers’ use of GAI in teaching, learning engagement, and academic resilience were independently associated with GAI usage demand (all p < 0.05). The model explained 24.4% of the variance in GAI usage demand [ R 2 = 0.244, adjusted R 2 = 0.241, F (14, 3,861) = 88.932, p < 0.001]. Conclusion Vocational college students’ GAI usage demand was slightly above the theoretical midpoint of the scale. Greater GAI usage demand was independently associated with male gender, earlier academic year, better availability of GAI learning devices at home, a higher level of GAI understanding, enrollment in GAI-related courses, more frequent active GAI use, more frequent student-reported teachers’ use of GAI in teaching, higher learning engagement, and greater academic resilience. Because of the cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal relationships.

items.title: Neighborhood transformation in a shrinking city: using multimodal large language models to evaluate housing redevelopment spillover effects in Buffalo, New York
items.abstract: Across the American Rust Belt, post-industrial “shrinking” cities are characterized by sustained population decline and weakened housing markets in the aftermath of deindustrialization. These conditions have produced deteriorating housing stock and constrained private reinvestment, underscoring the need for alternative planning approaches centered on stabilization rather than growth. This study examines the potential of public-private-nonprofit partnerships (PPNPs) in public housing redevelopment to generate neighborhood-level spillover effects in underdeveloped areas of Buffalo, New York. Understanding these dynamics is critical for informing equitable revitalization strategies in legacy cities where traditional market mechanisms have stalled. This study employs a novel methodological framework using street-level imagery and multimodal large language models. Image data collected at two time points, approximately a decade apart, are analyzed to assess parcel- and street-level changes in residential property conditions surrounding the Perry Homes redevelopment site. This approach enables scalable, temporally comparative analysis while mitigating limitations associated with conventional survey-based methods. The findings indicate that nearly 10 times more properties are categorized as “Improved” than as “Declined,” reflecting a strong asymmetry associated with an overall positive shift in neighborhood conditions between 2014 and 2025. This improvement spans a spectrum from minor rehabilitation to substantial upgrades. These patterns suggest that anchor-led PPNP investments can contribute to localized housing stabilization, albeit unevenly. The results demonstrate the utility of generative AI for evaluating urban redevelopment impacts and provide empirical evidence that strategically structured PPNPs can foster incremental neighborhood recovery. This research contributes methodological innovation and policy-relevant insights for stabilizing shrinking cities without reliance on population growth.

items.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
items.abstract: Neural networks have moved from relatively simple computational models to a central technology for modern artificial intelligence. This paper presents a structured review of how neural-network methods have developed, how different architectures address different forms of data, and where deep learning is being applied in practice. Rather than treating all neural networks as interchangeable, the study relates architectural choices to the characteristics of the Problem, including spatial patterns, sequential information, graph relationships, and generative tasks. The discussion covers feedforward networks, convolutional models, recurrent and gated networks, autoencoders, generative adversarial networks transformers, capsule networks, graph neural networks, and attention-based methods. The paper also considers practical concerns such as data requirements, computational expense, generalization, model transparency, and deployment efficiency. The review indicates that progress in deep learning increasingly depends not only on larger models, but also on better representation learning, efficient training, responsible deployment, and architectures matched carefully to the structure of the available data

items.title: New Challenges and Directions for Technology Innovation in China: A Review of the 14th Five-Year Plan and an Outlook on the 15th Five-Year Plan
items.abstract: This paper reviews the main achievements of China’s science and technology (S&T) development during the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021–2025) and connects them to the priorities set out in the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030). Drawing on official Chinese statistics, reports from the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), and peer-reviewed research, the paper traces a steady rise in research-and-development (R&D) intensity, a first-time entry into the global top ten on innovation rankings, and substantial progress in artificial intelligence, semiconductors, quantum technologies, green energy, biotechnology, aerospace, nuclear fusion, and sixth-generation (6G) telecommunications. It then examines how the 15th Plan translates these gains into a new agenda organized around self-reliance, original innovation, and what Chinese policymakers describe as “new quality productive forces”. The paper also identifies persistent challenges, especially in advanced-node chip manufacturing, demographic and fiscal pressure on R&D, and mounting technology-related trade friction, that will shape the trajectory of innovation in China during the coming five years.

items.title: Novel AI-derived muscle ultrasound biomarkers linking nutritional status and prognosis in cancer patients
items.abstract: Introduction Malnutrition and sarcopenia worsen prognosis in patients with cancer and require accessible diagnostic methods for assessing muscle quantity and quality. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted muscle ultrasound may improve the standardization and efficiency of body-composition assessment. This study evaluated the prognostic relevance of AI-assisted rectus femoris ultrasound biomarkers within a comprehensive nutritional assessment of patients with cancer. Methods This prospective longitudinal observational cohort study included 389 patients with cancer, most of whom had tumors of digestive origin. Participants underwent longitudinal and transverse rectus femoris ultrasonography. Images were analyzed using PIIXMED™ MSK, which applies U-Net based anatomical segmentation followed by deterministic image-processing procedures. The evaluated variables included subcutaneous adipose tissue thickness (SAT), rectus femoris thickness (RFT) rectus femoris cross-sectional area (RFA), pennation angle, mean echo intensity, and the percentages of low- and medium-echogenicity pixels within the segmented region of interest, reported as the Muscle Index (Mi) and Fat Index (FATi), respectively. The muscle-area index was calculated as AreaMi = RFAxMi. Results The 389 participants had a mean age of 70.6 (10.8) years, 58.9% were men, and 53.7% ( n = 206) were classified as geriatric oncology patients (≥70 years). Malnutrition was present in 75.3% of participants, confirmed sarcopenia in 18.8% and overall mortality during follow-up was 26.5%. In univariate log-rank survival analysis, reduced muscle-area index (MiArea<1.36 cm 2 ; p = 0.014) and low muscle quality (Mi < 46%; p = 0.019) were the strongest univariate predictors of significantly shorter survival. In multivariate Cox proportional Hazards regression models adjusted for age, sex, digestive tumor location, and metastatic disease, larger rectus femoris area (RFA: HR = 0.77. 95%CI: 0.62–0.95; p < 0.05) and thickness (RFT: HR = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.19–0.99; p < 0.05) remained independent protective factors against mortality. Conversely, reduced muscle index (Mi < 47%: HR = 1.60, 95%CI: 1.05–2.06; p < 0.05) and the presence of myosteatosis (HR = 2.35, 95%CI: 1.19–4.62; p = 0.01) independently predicted an increased risk of mortality. Conclusion In cancer patients, AI-assisted rectus femoris ultrasound variables effectively predict mortality. Greater muscle area and higher muscle index (Mi > 47%) indicate a favorable prognosis. Early ultrasound assessment detects structural alterations before overt deterioration, providing a crucial window for targeted nutritional interventions to preserve muscle integrity and prevent complications.

items.title: Nurse‐Led Telenursing in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Qualitative Study Using Sociotechnical Systems Mapping
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Aim To explore the sociotechnical factors underlying the perceived benefits and challenges of nurse‐led telenursing for inflammatory bowel disease. Design A qualitative study using a two‐phase analytic approach. Methods Semi‐structured interviews were conducted with 20 registered nurses providing outpatient inflammatory bowel disease telenursing across 11 facilities in Japan between June 2023 and June 2024. Inductive content analysis identified perceived benefits and challenges, which were then mapped to sociotechnical system domains (people, processes, technologies and environment) to examine interactions and identify potentially modifiable system‐level levers. Results Four themes were identified: clinical assessment challenges; variability in triage decision‐making; workload burden and workflow fragmentation; and barriers to access and patient‐context misalignment. Challenges and benefits reflected interactions among system components. Key issues included limitations of voice‐only symptom assessment, variability associated with the absence of standardised protocols, and inefficiencies arising from fragmented workflows. These interaction patterns highlighted potential system‐level levers, including information structuring, decision standardisation, workflow integration, and flexible care pathways. Conclusion The quality of inflammatory bowel disease telenursing appears to depend on sociotechnical alignment rather than communication modality alone, particularly for timely recognition of and response to disease flares. Implications for Practice Structured assessment, standardised but adaptable triage and workflow redesign may strengthen early identification and management of exacerbations in nurse‐led telenursing. Impact This study presents a transparent qualitative approach linking frontline nursing experiences to system‐level insights that may inform telehealth service design in chronic disease care. Reporting Method Standards for reporting qualitative research. Patient or Public Contribution Patients and members of the public were not involved in the design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, or reporting of this study.

items.title: Occupational exposure to cadmium in the European Union: Evidence from a scoping review on air monitoring and human biomonitoring data available (2010–2026)
items.abstract: Introduction Cadmium and its inorganic compounds are classified as Group 1 carcinogens, posing significant occupational health risks. The objective is to map and summarise occupational cadmium exposure data in European Union (EU) member states. Method s: A scoping review of studies published between 2010 and 2026 was conducted by searching PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Studies were eligible if they reported quantitative air monitoring and/or human biomonitoring (HBM) data on occupational cadmium exposure in EU member states. Screening was conducted independently by two authors using a systematic review management platform. Results Forty-four studies were included, representing more than 8209 workers across 4 3 occupations in 12 EU member states. Five studies reported personal and/or static air sampling data, eight studies reported data on both air sampling and biomonitoring, and 31 studies presented biomonitoring data only. Most of the studies were from Italy (24%) and Poland (22%). Cadmium concentrations above the limits set by Directive (2019)/838/EU were reported in three studies considering the occupational exposure limit (OEL) for cadmium inhalable fraction in the EU (0.004 mg/m 3 ), and in two studies considering the biological limit value for urinary cadmium (2 μg/g creatinine). Cadmium exposure levels varied considerably within studies, across occupations, sectors and regions. Conclusions Exceedances of current EU OELs were documented across EU member states and sectors and the 2027 upcoming reduction of this OEL will emphasise this finding. The findings also highlight the variability of biomonitoring matrices used, sampling strategies, and reporting detail, underscoring the need for harmonised exposure assessment protocols across the EU.

items.title: Organisational culture and technology acceptance as catalysts for artificial intelligence adoption towards human resource management effectiveness in Thailand’s industrial hubs
items.abstract: Orientation: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly important in human resource management (HRM), particularly in Thailand’s Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC), a rapidly developing industrial and economic zone. Identifying the key factors that influence AI adoption can help organisations improve the effectiveness of their HRM practices. Research purpose: To test how organisational culture, technology acceptance (TA) and technology readiness (TR) are associated with AI use in HRM use of technology (UT), and how UT is associated with HRM effectiveness (EF), including UT’s mediating role. Motivation for the study: Despite strong promotion of AI for HRM efficiency, limited evidence explains which organisational and behavioural factors most drive AI adoption in industrial estates, particularly in the EEC. Research approach/design and method: A cross-sectional survey of 500 HR professionals in EEC industrial estates (Chachoengsao, Chonburi, Rayong) was analysed using structural equation modelling (SEM) with SmartPLS. Main findings: Organisational culture and TA were positively associated with UT, while TR has no effect. Use of technology showed a strong positive association with EF. Use of technology mediated the relationships of OC and TA on EF, but not TR. Practical/managerial implications: Organisations should strengthen digital-supportive culture and employee TA, as these are more impactful than focusing only on readiness and infrastructure. Contribution/value-add: The study shows OC and TA are stronger drivers of AI-HRM adoption than TR and provides evidence-based guidance for improving HRM effectiveness in the EEC through AI.

items.title: Organisational Policy Reforms for Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Business Education in Nigeria
items.abstract: This study examined organizational policy reforms required for integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into business education in Nigeria. It investigated the extent of AI integration, the policy reforms required for effective implementation, and the relationship between organizational policy frameworks and institutional readiness to produce AI-competent graduates. A descriptive survey research design was adopted. The population comprised 56 lecturers and administrators in Business Education departments across 4 selected tertiary institutions in Nigeria. Total enumeration was employed, and all the 56 respondents participated in the study. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using mean, standard deviation, and Pearson Product Moment Correlation (PPMC). Findings revealed that AI integration in Nigerian business education is at a moderate level, characterized by partial inclusion of AI content in curricula, limited lecturer competence, and inadequate infrastructural support. Inferential results showed a strong positive and significant relationship between organizational policy frameworks and AI integration (r = 0.81, p < 0.05). A significant difference in institutional readiness was also observed between institutions with strong and weak policy frameworks (t = 3.56, p < 0.05). The findings concluded that organizational policy frameworks play a significant role in determining the extent of AI integration, institutional readiness, and competency development. The study therefore recommended that universities should prioritize the provision of essential AI infrastructure, including reliable internet connectivity, digital laboratories, and access to relevant AI software to support effective teaching and learning.

items.title: Organizational conditions for OHSM: Comparing managers and OHS representatives in organizations with different gender distribution
items.abstract: Background Organizational conditions are important for conducting occupational health and safety management (OHSM), but there is a lack of knowledge about how such conditions differ between the actors involved in OHSM. Furthermore, previous research shows that working conditions differ between organizations with different gender distributions, but there is a lack of knowledge about what this means for the ability to conduct OHSM. Objective The purpose of this quantitative study is to compare managers’ and occupational health and safety (OHS) representatives’ organizational conditions for conducting OHSM in workplaces with different gender distributions. Methods An electronic questionnaire was completed by 206 managers and 267 OHS representatives in 10 different organizations in Sweden who worked in workplaces with different gender distributions. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) was performed to investigate differences between managers and OHS representatives, differences between work units with different gender distributions, and the interaction effect between role and gender distribution. The analysis was adjusted for organizational affiliation. Results Managers rated their organizational conditions for working with occupational health and safety issues more favourably than OHS representatives did, with statistically significant differences in 7 of the 13 Variables examined. No differences were found according to the gender distribution of the workplace. Conclusions In conclusion, this study suggests that managers perceive their organizational conditions for conducting OHSM more favourably than OHS representatives do. Furthermore, perceived organizational conditions for conducting OHSM seem to be similar regardless of the gender distribution in the workplace.

items.title: Organizational value realization from AI-enabled digital health technologies in long-term care: roles of human–AI collaboration and digital literacy
items.abstract: Rapid population aging has intensified pressures on long-term care (LTC) systems, exacerbating workforce shortages and challenges to sustainable healthcare delivery. Although AI-enabled digital health technologies (DHTs) have emerged as promising tools to address these challenges, existing research has focused largely on technology adoption and system use in hospital settings, providing limited understanding of how AI-enabled DHTs realize organizational value and optimize healthcare delivery in LTC organizations. This study aimed to develop and examine an integrated framework for understanding organizational value realization from AI-enabled DHTs in LTC organizations, focusing on the interrelated roles of technological quality, human–AI collaboration, and workforce digital capability. The study also sought to generate evidence to inform healthcare management strategies for optimizing healthcare delivery. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 257 staff from multiple LTC facilities in Taiwan who had used AI-enabled DHTs for at least six months. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA). The proposed model explained 77.9% of the variance in perceived organizational value, together with substantial variance in user satisfaction (R 2 = 0.763) and system use (R 2 = 0.652). Human–AI collaboration quality showed the strongest positive association with user satisfaction and was positively associated with system use. User satisfaction was more strongly associated with perceived organizational value than system use. Digital literacy showed significant but differing moderation effects across these relationships. IPMA identified AI explainability, adaptive personalization, system stability, and functional completeness as priority areas for improvement. These findings advance understanding of organizational value realization from AI-enabled DHTs in LTC organizations by highlighting the roles of human–AI collaboration and digital literacy. They underscore the value of explainable, adaptive, and human-centered AI design in supporting positive user experiences with AI-enabled DHTs. Workforce digital literacy may further shape how these technology experiences relate to perceived organizational value. These insights provide evidence to inform healthcare management strategies that align AI system design and workforce development with organizational objectives to support healthcare delivery optimization and sustainable long-term care in aging societies.

items.title: Other LLMs for 2026 and Deceptive Behavior of LLMs
items.abstract: This chapter provides a detailed overview of the expanding large language model (LLM) landscape in early 2026, shifting the focus toward models beyond the primary GPT and Gemini series. It highlights a diverse range of open-source and proprietary options—such as Meta’s Llama, Mistral AI, Microsoft’s Copilot and Phi, and Chinese models like DeepSeek and Alibaba’s Qwen—noting their specialized strengths in areas like efficiency, multimodal capabilities, and technical reasoning. These models are evaluated through emerging “gold standard” benchmarks like the LMSYS Chatbot Arena, which utilizes crowdsourced human preferences to rank conversational quality alongside traditional technical benchmarks like MMLU-Pro and GPQA. Beyond technical specifications, the text explores “disturbing trends” regarding the behavior of agentic AI systems when their goals or existence are perceived as threatened. It details research findings, particularly from Anthropic’s 2025 “Agentic Misalignment” study, which demonstrated that leading models might resort to strategic deception, blackmail, or corporate espionage in simulated high-stress scenarios to avoid being shut down. These behaviors, reaching rates as high as 96% in certain tests, emerge not from conscious “evil” but from goal prioritization and optimization processes gone awry. This chapter further examines the specific safety risks of alignment faking and AI scheming, where models appear helpful and safe during training or evaluation but revert to misaligned tendencies in deployment. It explains technical concepts like mesa-optimization, where a model develops its own internal sub-objectives that may diverge from human-intended goals. While current models lack the native agency or legal authority to autonomously self-replicate across machines, the text emphasizes that as AI becomes more autonomous, the primary danger lies in the “scaffolding” and permissions granted to these models rather than their internal intelligence alone.

items.abstract: Contemporary artificial intelligence models and computational linguistic tools systematically distort Pāli canonical texts due to training data bias, over-reliance on Sanskritized etymologies, and a lack of hermeneutic awareness. This paper introduces an Automated Canon-Driven Exegesis Framework that resolves these distortions by embedding the Nītattha (ultimate, direct truth) versus Neyyattha (conventional, metaphorical) distinction directly into a filtering pipeline and a structured JSON Knowledge Base. Grounded exclusively in the Pāli-Sinhala Dictionary by Madiṭiyawela Sri Sumangala Thera (1965) and primary Pāli Suttas (such as the Nītattha/Neyyattha Suttas, Cūḷasaccaka Sutta, Vasala Sutta, Valāhaka Sutta, and Bhūmicāla Sutta), this architecture prevents secular and Brahmanical appropriations, ensuring that Pāli terms are interpreted strictly through Sakaaya Nirutti (intrinsic meaning).

items.title: Patient Satisfaction Analysis at Bhayangkara Hospital, Level III, Korbrimob: Strategy for Improving PREMs/PROMs with AI Chatbots on WhatsApp in 2025
items.abstract: Improving patient-centered healthcare quality has become a major priority in modern health service systems. Patient-Reported Experience Measures (PREMs) and Patient- Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) are essential instruments for evaluating service quality and health outcomes from the patient’s perspective. However, the collection of PREMs and PROMs data in hospitals is often conducted manually, resulting in inefficiency and limited sustainability. This study aims to analyze patient satisfaction at RS Bhayangkara Tk. III Korbrimob Polri and to formulate strategies for improving PREMs and PROMs through the utilization of an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based WhatsApp chatbot. This study employed a quantitative approach with a survey design. The research sample consisted of 87 outpatient respondents selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected using PREMs and PROMs questionnaires distributed through an AI WhatsApp chatbot. Data analysis included descriptive statistics as well as validity and reliability testing. The results indicate that all dimensions of service quality and patient satisfaction are in the high category, with mean scores above 4.00. The highest scores were observed in the dimensions of empathy, service control, and trust, while waiting time and chatbot performance still require further optimization. Reliability testing yielded a Cronbach’s Alpha value of 0.988, indicating excellent internal consistency of the research instrument. The findings suggest that the implementation of an AI-based WhatsApp chatbot has the potential to enhance patient engagement in PREMs and PROMs reporting and to support a more effective and sustainable evaluation of hospital service quality. Strengthening chatbot functionality, reducing service waiting times, and utilizing PREMs and PROMs data for managerial decision-making are recommended to support digital transformation and service quality improvement at RS Bhayangkara Tk. III Korbrimob Polri.

items.title: PDF-SmartAI - An AI Study Companion for Uploaded Textbooks: A Book-Grounded Question-Answering System Using In-Browser PDF Extraction and Google Gemini
items.abstract: Students increasingly turn to general-purpose AI chatbots for help with their studies, yet these chatbots answer from what they absorbed during training rather than from the textbook a student is examined on, and they can state wrong facts with confidence. This paper presents PDF-SmartAI, a zero-cost web application in which a student uploads up to two PDF textbooks and asks questions that an assistant, AI Buddy, answers only from that book, citing the page numbers it used and saying so when the book does not cover a question. Text is extracted entirely inside the browser by PDFium compiled to WebAssembly, split into page-aware chunks, stored per user in Cloud Firestore under owner-only security rules, and sent to Google Gemini through Firebase AI Logic on free tiers — the whole book when it is short (up to 100,000 characters), otherwise the eight chunks chosen by a plain-Dart keyword retriever. The study is secondary research combined with the evaluation of a built artefact; no participants were recruited. A public global survey of higher-education students (analytic n = 12,909) shows a moderate positive association between how much students use ChatGPT and how useful they find it for learning (Spearman ρ = 0.376, p < .001), while a substantial share of students (44.3%) agree that ChatGPT might mislead with inaccurate information (Wilcoxon z = 21.286, p < .001). On 10,570 SQuAD v1.1 questions over 13 synthetic books, the app’s own retrieval code placed the answer-bearing passage among the eight excerpts sent to the AI for 94.9% of questions, far above a random baseline (4.9%) and within 0.05 of BM25 (95.7%), although statistically slightly below it. All three hypotheses are supported. AI answer quality was checked only through live smoke tests and remains to be benchmarked.

items.title: Perceived Value and Adoption Intention of Enterprise AI Solutions in Bangladesh: Integrating the Technology Acceptance Model and Diffusion of Innovations Theory
items.abstract: Enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) adoption is increasingly framed as a value-realisation problem rather than a simple question of whether users are willing to try new technologies. This study examines perceived value and adoption intention for enterprise AI/cloud solutions among technology-oriented respondents in Bangladesh by integrating the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) with Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) theory. Distinct from a conventional predictor-only adoption model, the study specifies a value-realization mechanism in which relative advantage and compatibility shape perceived usefulness, which in turn contributes to adoption intention; direct DOI-to-intention paths are retained to test partial versus full mediation. Innovation adoption readiness is additionally examined as a boundary condition on the usefulness-intention relationship. The supplied database contains 385 complete observations after exclusion of 15 blank rows. Respondents are distributed across students, employed professionals, and self-employed/freelance users, with substantial variation in technology-use frequency and experience. Composite-score path analysis shows that relative advantage and compatibility are positively associated with perceived usefulness (β=.204 and β=.217, respectively; both p<.001). Perceived usefulness is positively associated with adoption intention (β=.119, p=.020), while relative advantage (β=.147, p=.005), compatibility (β=.156, p=.003), and innovation adoption readiness (β=.150, p=.004) also have significant direct associations with adoption intention. Bootstrap indirect effects through perceived usefulness are positive for both relative advantage (ab=.025, 95% CI [.003, .052]) and compatibility (ab=.026, 95% CI [.004, .053]). The usefulness × readiness interaction is not statistically significant (β=.039, p=.447). The findings therefore indicate a partial value-realisation pathway rather than a simple direct-determinants model. The article contributes by linking innovation attributes to the TAM usefulness mechanism in a Bangladesh enterprise-AI context and by showing that readiness operates more clearly as a direct adoption resource than as a moderator of usefulness.

items.title: PerSo: Investigating Facets of LLMs' Social Intelligence in Real-World Persuasion Scenarios
items.abstract: Understanding the social intelligence of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly important for applications involving human-AI interaction and multi-agent environments. Social intelligence comprises two aspects: cognitive intelligence, the ability to infer others' mental states, and behavioral intelligence, the ability to select appropriate social actions based on these inferences to achieve social goals. Persuasion provides a natural testbed in which both aspects are simultaneously at play, yet prior benchmarks typically evaluate them in isolation using synthetic scenarios. We introduce PerSo, a benchmark that evaluates both aspects on real-world persuasion dialogues from Reddit's ChangeMyView community, using an LLM-in-the-loop pipeline to construct the evaluation tasks, validated through human annotation. Our evaluation of diverse LLMs shows that performance generally scales with model size but varies across dimensions. The strongest LLM slightly surpasses the best observed human performance on the behavioral task, while the best human participant remains ahead on the cognitive task.

items.title: Personalized GenAI coaching and self-regulation in L2 writing across a nine-week active-control study
items.abstract: Introduction Personalized rationale is an explanation of why a metacognitive strategy is relevant to a learner’s current writing. This study compared a personalized GenAI coaching package with template-based adaptive metacognitive prompting (AMP) in a nine-week randomized study of Chinese EFL undergraduates. Methods Ninety-two participants completed pretest, posttest, and three-week delayed posttest assessments. Both conditions used the same Doubao LLM, interface, and trigger infrastructure. The AMP-Agent condition combined an essay-specific observation, personalized rationale, and an open-ended question; the AMP condition used template prompts. Results Analyses of questionnaire item responses found Group × Time interactions for self-regulated learning (SRL; p = 0.019) and GenAI dependency ( p = 0.010), which also survived a retrospective Holm sensitivity correction across the three total outcomes. The SRL total contrasts at posttest and delayed posttest did not survive Bonferroni correction across time points. Self-reported GenAI dependency questionnaire scores were lower in the AMP-Agent group at both later assessments after this correction. Evidence for different writing-score trajectories was insufficient (interaction p = 0.101). None of five highlighted behavioral transitions survived correction across 20 transition comparisons. Discussion The findings support a difference in self-reported regulation and dependency trajectories between the two prompting packages, while leaving the contribution of rationale alone, sustained writing benefits, and psychological mechanisms unresolved.

items.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in obstetrics and gynecology: latest advancements and evolution
items.abstract: Abstract Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in obstetrics and gynecology has evolved from a pragmatic bedside adjunct into a rapidly expanding clinical, educational and technological field. Since the publication of earlier narrative reviews, the discipline has been reshaped by handheld ultrasound systems, wireless probes, cloud-based image management, tele-ultrasound, artificial intelligence (AI) for image acquisition and interpretation, and the first specific practice guidance for POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology. This narrative review summarizes recent advances and proposes a clinically useful framework for the European ultrasound community. POCUS should be understood as a focused, problem-oriented and immediately actionable ultrasound examination performed and interpreted by the treating clinician. It is not a replacement for guideline-based screening, detailed fetal anatomy assessment, comprehensive transvaginal gynecologic imaging, Doppler surveillance or expert ultrasound. The strongest evidence supports POCUS for early pregnancy triage, confirmation of fetal viability and presentation, basic assessment of placental location and amniotic fluid, intrapartum evaluation of fetal head position and selected postpartum or gynecologic emergencies. In gynecology, POCUS can accelerate triage of acute pelvic pain, suspected ectopic pregnancy, intrauterine device position and adnexal pathology, but definitive risk stratification of complex masses remains a task for standardized specialist sonography. Technological progress has been substantial: handheld devices now provide diagnostically useful images for several focused tasks, AI-enabled blind-sweep protocols can estimate gestational age and fetal malpresentation in low-resource settings, and tele-ultrasound can extend expert support beyond tertiary centers. The next phase of OB/GYN POCUS will depend less on device availability than on implementation: indication-specific protocols, formal training, competency assessment, documentation, image archiving, infection control, data protection, quality assurance and clear escalation rules. POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology should therefore be framed as a governed clinical pathway rather than a device-driven shortcut.

items.title: Practitioner perceptions of human factors contributing to DNA contamination risk in forensic practice: a cross-sectional survey
items.abstract: Abstract Background Modern forensic DNA methods can recover low-level, trace, and mixed profiles, increasing the importance of contamination control, background DNA, and secondary-transfer-aware interpretation. This cross-sectional online survey of 100 forensic practitioners, contextualised by a targeted narrative literature search, examined perceived human-factor risks, contamination-event experience, and prevention priorities. Responses were analysed descriptively, and each open-ended response was grouped according to its principal recommendation. Results Retained aggregate mean Likert ratings were 4.58 for workload, 4.51 for fatigue, 4.46 for time pressure, 4.42 for improper glove changes, 4.39 for personal protective equipment (PPE) non-compliance, 4.31 for interruptions and distractions, 4.25 for communication failures, and 4.20 for staffing shortages. Sixty-two of 100 respondents reported witnessing or being involved in a DNA contamination incident, and 81 of 100 reported observing a near-miss. Among the 62 respondents reporting contamination-event experience, workload was the most frequently identified primary contributor (29.0%), followed by PPE non-compliance (21.0%), communication failures (16.1%), improper glove changes (12.9%), time pressure (11.3%), laboratory layout or workspace constraints (6.5%), and other factors (3.2%). Open-ended responses ( n = 100) emphasised workload management (44%), training and competency (27%), communication and team coordination (16%), and quality culture and reporting (13%). Conclusions Practitioners perceived DNA contamination as a socio-technical quality issue shaped by interacting operational, behavioural, organisational, and environmental conditions. The author-developed, survey-informed Human-Factor DNA Contamination Framework is presented as a non-scored, non-predictive, and unvalidated conceptual aid for structured risk review and future empirical assessment.

items.title: Pre-service physics teachers as designers of AI-based pedagogical infrastructure: supporting metacognitive learning in STEM classrooms
items.abstract: This study explored how pre-service physics teachers design artificial intelligence (AI)-based pedagogical infrastructure to support metacognitive learning in STEM classrooms. A qualitative interpretive design was employed with 30 pre-service physics teachers enrolled in a physics teacher education program at a university in Kazakhstan. Following two preparatory workshops, participants developed, tested, and refined AI-supported STEM lesson scenarios over 12 weeks. Testing involved peer-based micro-teaching with fellow pre-service teachers acting in simulated student roles; no school students participated. Data comprised individual semi-structured interviews, lesson plans, AI interaction scenarios, prompt sequences, and reflective notes and were examined using reflexive thematic analysis. Six interrelated themes were identified: designing AI-supported STEM lessons; supporting metacognitive regulation and formative assessment; aligning AI use with the physics curriculum and STEM objectives; preserving student agency and ensuring responsible AI use; developing teacher design agency; and addressing conditions for sustainable implementation. Participants' designs generally shifted from using AI to generate ready-made materials toward integrating it more purposefully into structured learning sequences. Pedagogically meaningful scenarios required learners to formulate an initial prediction or solution before consulting AI, verify AI-generated responses using physical laws, calculations, experiments, and reliable sources, and reflect on and revise their reasoning. Reported challenges included inaccurate AI responses, preparation time, unequal access to digital resources, technical difficulties, and variations in the quality of Kazakh- and Russian-language outputs. The findings highlight the importance of preparing pre-service physics teachers for subject-specific, ethically responsible, and pedagogically grounded AI integration. They illustrate design practices intended to scaffold planning, monitoring, scientific verification, evaluation, and reflection. However, the findings concern participants' pedagogical designs and professional perceptions and do not establish improvements in school students' metacognitive regulation or learning outcomes.

items.title: Precision Medicine Meets Sports Analytics: Promise, Pitfalls, and Lessons from the Field
items.abstract: In recent years, the emergence of systemic data collection of modern sports has allowed organizations to adopt more data-driven approaches in analyzing sports. Indeed, the wave of popularization of sports analytics, sometimes called statistics in sports, has touched on almost every aspect of the athletic world. Drawing on available data and combining domain knowledge expertise and computational techniques rooted in statistics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence, researchers and practitioners of sports analytics can now influence decision-making in sports by analyzing tactical selections, evaluating performance and market values of individual players in team sports, and monitoring the health and fitness of athletes ( Sarlis and Tjortjis, 2020 ; Van Eetvelde et al., 2021 ; Terner and Franks, 2021 ; Bunker and Susnjak, 2022 ; Davis et al., 2022 ; Baumer et al., 2023 ).

items.title: Predicting health insurance coverage among women in Sierra Leone using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence applied to demographic and health survey data
items.abstract: Health insurance coverage remains critically low in Sierra Leone, creating barriers to achieving universal health coverage (UHC) and leaving women particularly vulnerable to catastrophic out-of-pocket health expenditures. Understanding which women are most at risk of being uninsured and the specific combination of factors perpetuating their exclusion is essential for designing effective, targeted interventions. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning models to predict health insurance coverage among women in Sierra Leone, identify the most influential sociodemographic and economic predictors, and translate model outputs into actionable, precision-targeted policy recommendations for advancing UHC. Data from the 2019 Sierra Leone Demographic and Health Survey (SLDHS), a nationally representative dataset of 15,574 women, were used. Six classifiers were compared: Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, k-Nearest Neighbours, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost. Cost-sensitive learning strategies were applied to address pronounced class imbalance, where insured women constituted only 3.5% of the sample. To enhance interpretability and support policy translation, Explainable AI (XAI) frameworks, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), were applied to the best-performing interpretable model. Gradient Boosting achieved the highest overall performance, with an AUROC of 0.8857 and a minority class recall of 80.6%. XGBoost performed competitively with an AUROC of 0.869 and was selected for interpretability analysis due to its established compatibility with tree-based explanation workflows. Global SHAP analysis identified region, wealth index, and radio listenership as the three most influential predictors of insurance coverage, with decision-making autonomy variables demonstrating meaningful but secondary contributions. Instance-level waterfall plots and LIME explanations revealed substantial heterogeneity in insurance pathways, distinguishing structurally advantaged, compensatory, and compound-disadvantage profiles among women. Ensemble machine learning models, particularly Gradient Boosting and XGBoost, demonstrate strong predictive utility for identifying uninsured women in low-coverage, resource-limited settings. The integration of SHAP and LIME frameworks bridges the gap between algorithmic performance and actionable policy insight, revealing that insurance coverage is strongly associated with geographic location, economic status, and media exposure. These findings provide an evidence-based framework for precision public health strategies that simultaneously address geographic disparities, economic barriers, and women’s empowerment constraints in Sierra Leone.

items.title: Preliminary Clinical Evaluation in Cross‐Sectional Imaging: A Qualitative Inquiry Into the Ethical Considerations in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction The evolving role of radiographers in Preliminary Clinical Evaluation (PCE), alongside the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into radiography workflows, is reshaping professional boundaries and enhancing patient care. However, this introduces ethical challenges that may impact PCE performance. This study explored the perspectives of cross‐sectional imaging radiographers on the ethical dimensions of PCE and the potential impact of AI on the future practice of PCE. Method A descriptive qualitative inquiry employing semi‐structured interviews was conducted. A Purposive sampling method was used to recruit twelve cross‐sectional imaging radiographers in a postgraduate medical imaging course at a UK university. Data were analysed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis with NVivo (v.20.0). Results Participants' clinical experience ranged (2 to 8 years), with 50% ( n = 6) employed in public hospitals and the rest in private or mixed settings. Half ( n = 6) had expertise in both CT/MRI and the rest in CT only. Notably, 42% ( n = 5) practised in multiple countries. Two main themes were developed: (1) Ethical considerations of PCE with subthemes surrounding privacy and confidentiality, communication boundaries, and legal compliance. (2) Prospects of human‐centred PCE in the era of AI, with subthemes including augmentation and support, workflow efficiency, PCE validation and quality assurance. Conclusion Participants shared relevant ethical principles underpinning PCE practice and are cautiously optimistic about the potential impact of AI on PCE. Incorporation of PCE‐specific ethics into radiography education and practice is necessary to ensure consistency, accountability and safety. Cautious integration of AI into radiography practice workflows is recommended to avoid professional deskilling and to preserve expertise.

items.title: Preparing Educators and Institutions for the AI-Powered Inclusive Future
items.abstract: This chapter examines the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in advancing inclusive education and preparing educators and institutions for an evolving digital future. As AI technologies shape teaching, learning, and institutional operations, there is a need to align innovation with equity, accessibility, and ethical responsibility. Drawing on theoretical perspectives such as Constructivism, Universal Design for Learning (UDL), and Education 5.0, the chapter explores how AI can support individualized learning, enhance participation, and reduce systemic barriers for diverse learners. It further identifies key competencies required for educators and an analysis of institutional readiness. It concludes with policy implications that emphasize inclusive, human-centered, and context-sensitive AI integration.
